A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the WallFacer training system despite changes to the title and byline. All pages, equations, figures, and tables support comparison. Both documents end with references and contain no separate appendices.

before.justification: v1 Section 5 and Figures 7–10 report original throughput, memory-consumption, and strong/weak-scaling measurements for GPT training.

after.justification: v3 Section 4 retains GPT measurements and adds original DiT throughput, memory-consumption, and scaling results.

M1.justification: The QKV replication, multi-ring attention, configuration generator, grid-search scheduler, causal/full-mask loading, and checkpointing procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 now receives initial peer ranks as arguments, while their construction remains documented in the same configuration algorithms; this does not establish a changed training method.

E1.justification: v1 benchmarks GPT 3B/7B language-model training. v3 adds 1B DiT backbone training representing the computer-vision/image-generation setting, with throughput, memory, and scaling evaluations in Figures 7–10. This substantially broadens evaluated task coverage, although the DiT setup excludes text and image encoders.

E2.justification: Ring Attention remains the evaluated comparator. New Table 4 also compares against Ring Attention, using capacity values attributed to its paper. Ulysses, Megatron sequence parallelism, DistFlashAttention, and FlashAttention3 are discussed without added comparative experiments.

E3.justification: v3 adds DiT scaling on 8–32 GPUs: fixed 128K sequences for strong scaling and 128–512K for weak scaling, with inter-node communication throughout. Table 4 adds capacity checks on one A100 80GB GPU. The stated GPT 3B configuration changes from 12 layers/16 heads in v1 Section 5 to 16 layers/12 heads in v3 Table 3; rerunning is not established. Core metrics, batch size, and GPT scaling protocols remain.

E4.justification: v3 expands the memory-limit analysis from v1 Section 5.2's qualitative statement into Table 4's explicit feasibility grid for 3B/7B/13B models at 128/256/512K tokens. This supplies additional evidence about whether QKV replication reduces supported sequence length. Existing configuration and scaling analyses are also extended to DiT.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added plots retain the earlier practice of reporting bars without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds DiT throughput advantages of 114.33% at 128K and 41.4% at 512K, together with DiT memory/scaling results and Table 4's capacity outcomes. The stated GPT maxima of 77.12% throughput improvement and 60.71% strong-scaling improvement on 64 GPUs remain. The substantial additions concern new experimental conditions rather than version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.1's formal n-body definition and attention mapping, including Equations 2–3 and the forward/backward formulation, are removed without appendix relocation. The communication and memory-cost derivations remain in v3 Section 3.2.2. v3 also adds a brief quadratic-work argument explaining expected DiT weak-scaling throughput.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion withdraw attention-as-n-body as a standalone novel contribution and refocus the paper on the training system. They expand the demonstrated efficiency claim to both GPT/NLP and DiT/CV, adding the 114.33% DiT headline while retaining the central multi-ring communication-efficiency claim.

C2.justification: v3 Section 5 adds hypotheses about increased relevance with FlashAttention3 and compatibility with other parallelisms, including Ulysses. Section 4.3 interprets DiT weak scaling through approximately constant expected throughput. Section 4.2 qualifies the memory-overhead range with an exception for DiT 512K Wall-4. The core communication–memory tradeoff interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies 100Gbps Ethernet and the DiT architecture/backbone setup in Tables 2–3 and Section 4. Figure 1 loses v1's explicit Llama-7B, 64-GPU, Adam, batch-size-4 context. Runtime details largely remain, but Section 5.1 introduces an FP16 description that conflicts with the retained bfloat16 experimental setting.

R1.justification: v3 substantially contracts v1's n-body and methodology-transfer positioning, removing much of the hierarchical-method and parallel-matrix-algorithm lineage while retaining Driscoll et al. as inspiration. It adds GPT, Stable Diffusion 3, and FlashAttention3 references and develops complementary positioning with Ulysses. The DiT paper itself was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, the standalone formulation section is removed, and a new Discussion section is introduced. Background and motivation are reorganized, many explanatory paragraphs are revised, and author/byline information changes.

P2.justification: Communication diagrams are redrawn, charts are restyled, and Tables 2–4 are added. Figures 7–8 expand from six to eight panels, while Figures 9–10 combine retained GPT plots with new DiT panels. Figure captions, fonts, placement, and document layout also change extensively.

improvement.justification: The DiT throughput and scaling experiments provide useful support for applicability beyond GPT, while the focused motivation clarifies the communication mechanism and Table 4 makes capacity claims explicit. The core algorithm and cost analysis remain available despite removal of the n-body formalization. Gains are tempered by the unexplained 3B head/layer reversal and conflicting FP16/bfloat16 descriptions, which limit reproducibility. Overall, the evidence supports a limited net improvement.
